Multiple roles of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) in skeletal development, growth, and repair. Publisher Summary This chapter discusses the developmental roles of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) in skeletal morphogenesis, speculates on the future directions of research in this area, and describes some of the challenges in the field. VEGF regulates osteoclastic differentiation, migration, and activity. VEGF is, therefore, a key coordinator of the entire process. VEGF is necessary for osteoclastic activity both at the stage when the primary ossification center is established and later during bone growth.
